title: Intracranial entrainment reveals statistical learning across levels of abstraction (Sherman et al., 2023): raw iEEG from 8 neurosurgical patients
description: Raw intracranial EEG (iEEG) recorded from 8 neurosurgical patients with electrodes implanted for seizure monitoring while they viewed rapid streams of scene photographs. Streams contained statistical structure at either the category or exemplar level, plus a random baseline condition, allowing neural entrainment to learned structure to be examined across levels of abstraction. The data are converted to iEEG-BIDS from the original Dryad release without signal modification.
methods_description: Recordings used a Natus NeuroWorks EEG system sampled at 4096 Hz, with a reference electrode chosen by the clinical team to minimize noise. Scene images were shown for 250 ms followed by a 250 ms inter-stimulus interval. Triggers from a custom DAQ were inserted as 8-bit codes into an open EEG channel (TRIG), and events were decoded from this channel.
